messages.author: e715a3aeb27b07f3
messages.subject: coordinate system question
parts:
Hi there,

I was wondering whether there is any way to combine coord_trans and
coord_equal. I have a matrix of values and I'd like to display it with
geom_tile. I'd like to have the fixed width of x and y (to get a nice
heatmap with squares). But additionally, my data has it's origin at
the upper left corner. So data point (1,1) would be the upper left
corner; data point (8,1) would be below. If I use coord_trans with
reverse for y-values I get this as a result but the fixed ratio of
coord_equal is gone. Is there any solution for this problem?

A

messages.author: affa918ed63b6275
messages.subject: Re: coordinate system question
parts:
Hi, try this:

d <- data.frame(expand.grid(x=1:8, y=1:8))
d$z <- d$y
p <- ggplot(d, aes(x, y, fill=z)) + geom_tile() +
scale_y_continuous(trans="reverse") + coord_equal()
print(p)

--

messages.author: affa918ed63b6275
messages.subject: Re: coordinate system question
parts:
Hi, perhaps these will be changed in the next version of ggplot2, but you can do it by:

TransLogrev <- Trans$new("logrev", function(x) -log(x), function(x) exp(-x), function(x) exp(-x))


d <- data.frame(x = rlnorm(1000))

p <- ggplot(d, aes(x)) + stat_density() + 

  scale_x_continuous(trans="logrev")

print(p)


--
